Risk: Model systematically under-scores an already under-served subgroup, so they get less proactive outreach
Threat / Source: Historical care-access gaps encoded in the training data
Vulnerability / Condition: No subgroup performance analysis yet; proxy signals may leak through correlated features
Existing Controls: None effective yet. Decision B (no demographic proxies as inputs; sensitive attributes held only for measurement) is a design choice, not yet built.
Scoring Rationale: L4: care-access disparities in training data are common and would go uncaught without the MEASURE work. I4: a systematically under-served group getting even less proactive care is a serious equity and safety harm plus Art. 10 exposure. Revisit after the bias assessment; may fall if subgroup performance is clean and monitored.

Risk: Scores are unreliable because feature extracts are incomplete or stale
Vulnerability / Condition: No input data-quality checks before scoring
Scoring Rationale: L4: EHR extract gaps are routine and there is no pre-scoring validation. I3: unreliable scores misdirect outreach, but a clinician still decides and no care is denied.

Risk: Clinicians defer to the ranked list and stop exercising independent judgement, so patients the model does not flag are neglected
Threat / Source: Time pressure; the score is presented as authoritative
Vulnerability / Condition: Oversight design not workflow-tested; recommendation-only framing not deployed
Affected Parties: Patients not flagged by the model
Existing Controls: None effective yet. The 'decision support, not a clinical judgement' framing is decided (system description s7) but not built or tested with clinicians.
Scoring Rationale: L4: automation bias in clinical decision support under time pressure is well evidenced. I4: patients who are not surfaced and then deteriorate represent missed care and potential serious harm.

Risk: A clinician cannot sense-check a score and so cannot catch a wrong one
Threat / Source: Tree ensemble; only the top features are shown
Vulnerability / Condition: The explanation may be insufficient for the decision context
Existing Controls: Top-contributing-features display is designed (s5, s7), not built.
Scoring Rationale: L3: whether top features plus a data link is enough to sense-check a score is untested. I3: a wrong score acted on misdirects outreach; bounded by the human decision and overlapping with AR-03.

Risk: Model performance decays as the population or coding practice changes and the decay is not noticed
Threat / Source: No retraining trigger; no post-market monitoring
Existing Controls: None. Retraining cadence is defined (s6) but no monitoring is in place to trigger it.
Scoring Rationale: L4: drift is near certain over time for a clinical risk model. I3: prioritisation quality degrades gradually and could run undetected for months without monitoring.

Risk: Feature data or scores for named patients are exposed
Threat / Source: Misconfigured S3 or IAM on the meridian-ai footprint, as seen in the Cloud Risk Assessment lab
Vulnerability / Condition: The lab's remediation patterns are not yet applied to this footprint
Existing Controls: None specific to this footprint. The Cloud Risk Assessment lab's controls and lessons are available to apply.
Scoring Rationale: L3: a fresh build with the lab's lessons available, but the same account previously carried real misconfigurations. I4: exposure of health-related features and scores for identifiable patients is a confidential-data breach with GDPR and contractual consequences.

Risk: Affected patients are unaware that an AI system influences their care prioritisation
Vulnerability / Condition: Art. 13 transparency and GDPR Arts. 13 to 14 duties depend on deployment of the notice (AIA-05)
Existing Controls: Decision A made: patients are to be informed via the partner clinic's layered privacy notice. Not yet deployed.
Scoring Rationale: L3: the notice is decided but not in place, so today patients are not told. I3: a transparency and lawful-processing failure with trust harm, but no direct physical harm.

Risk: The override and reorder path exists but is not usable under real clinical workload, so oversight is nominal
Threat / Source: Oversight not workflow-tested with clinician users
Existing Controls: One-click dismiss and reorder is designed (s7), not validated in a real workflow.
Scoring Rationale: L3: plausible that the override path is clunky under load; unknown until tested. I4: if oversight is theatre, clinicians cannot correct a wrong model output and patient harm follows. Overlaps AR-03; kept separate because the fix is workflow validation, not framing.

Risk: A defect or licence problem in the model container or a dependency affects scores or the right to operate
Vulnerability / Condition: No component inventory or licence review (part of AIA-08)
Existing Controls: None. Uses the AWS-provided XGBoost container and standard libraries.
Scoring Rationale: L2: a defect or licence issue in well-used components is possible but not likely. I3: a dependency defect could distort scores; a licence issue is a legal and operational problem.
